chapter: Retirement and the future of big bands
title: Clark Terry's account of joining the band on the air
summary: Barnet confirms putting Terry on the spot by introducing him live, after trusting Charlie Shavers's recommendation.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: I presume that you are familiar with Clarke Terry's account of his joining your band, the first time he played a solo? It was in Stanley Dance's book, the interview with Clarke Terry. Do you know -- do you remember this? Clarke says, 'Charlie Barnet called me from California while I was working the Riviera, a big plush sort of place where Ellington swears he originally wrote, 'Sophisticated Lady.' I didn't know a soul in Charlie's band and the only person I knew in L.A. was Gerald Wilson. He took me over to where the band was playing and I walked up to the bandstand. The band was on the air and Charlie motioned me to go around the back and onto the stand. The next thing he was announcing, 'Now we'll hear from our new trumpet player, Clarke Terry, who has just arrived'. It was one of his originals, 'Charleston Alley,'

or something like that, and it wasn't too difficult, but it was a big chance to take, on the air, coast to coast. Ellington does things like that too. I stayed with the band for one of the happiest years of my life, until Charlie got lonesome for his swimming pools, private plane and yacht. Charlie's the most wonderful person in the world."

I have to come back and say Clarke is the most wonderful person in the world. I think something like that did happen. But I used to enjoy putting people on the spot like that, particularly when I knew they were perfectly capable of handling it.
But the story really did remind me of -- it's the kind of thing Duke would do. And usually a person who's very capable, even if they're terrified, will come through, because of that pressure.
But did you know how good Clarke was, really?

I hadn't heard him play, but I had complete faith in Charlie Shavers, and I mean, I talked a great deal -- when you go and send for a guy from St. Louis -- I had talked very long with Charlie about Clarke, and after what he said and as much faith as I had in Charlie, I had no qualms about it at all.
